raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil — heavy clay loam, decent fertility but needs good management. We've had less rain lately, good thing I have the well. My wife and I work this farm ourselves, so I keep things practical. No fancy experiments at my age.

My 16.1 mu breaks down the way it always has: about 9 mu on the wheat-maize rotation and 7.1 mu of cotton. Cotton prices have been decent and I know how to grow it here. The wheat-maize land doubles up — wheat goes in October, maize follows right after the wheat harvest in June with no-till to save time and moisture.

For wheat, I'll plough deep before sowing — I've always done this and my yields hold up. I use the improved variety from the county seed station, not the old local stuff. Three irrigations: before freeze, jointing, heading. Two rounds of pesticide — herbicide early, then something for rust if it shows up. Fertilizer at rates I've settled on over the years.

For maize, I drill straight into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed, everyone here uses it now. Two irrigations if summer rains are short. Lighter on pesticide than the cotton.

Cotton is the labor-heavy one. Bt hybrid cuts bollworm pressure but I still spray six times — aphids and spider mites come every year no matter what. Three irrigations timed to boll development. I top-dress nitrogen twice through the season.
